This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via crm_lead (literal, a string literal in fixture))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via crm_lead (literal, a string literal in fixture))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object translationLocaleTagCanonicalized), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object translationLocaleTagCanonicalized), crm_lead (literal, a string literal in fixture))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a4eae06499a8f0377960bfc9c98daced5cf19258` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bdce2f25ec6274740bc3d40393edd9acc1870954` — the merge of head `2f0b44d58376c8b5377f865e09570a2dc744a844` into base `a4eae06499a8f0377960bfc9c98daced5cf19258`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bdce2f25ec6274740bc3d40393edd9acc1870954 && git checkout bdce2f25ec6274740bc3d40393edd9acc1870954
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a4eae06499a8f0377960bfc9c98daced5cf19258 2f0b44d58376c8b5377f865e09570a2dc744a844 && git checkout -B drift-repro a4eae06499a8f0377960bfc9c98daced5cf19258 && git merge --no-ff 2f0b44d58376c8b5377f865e09570a2dc744a844

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a4eae06499a8f0377960bfc9c98daced5cf19258
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a4eae06499a8f0377960bfc9c98daced5cf19258` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.translation-locale-non-tag-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/system/translation.test.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts, .changeset/25822-locale-tag-shape.md, packages/spec/src/conversions/types.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts, packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/value-domain.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/seed-loader.zod.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-i18n.ts, packages/core/src/fallbacks/authored-translation-sync.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts

Narrowing face: the PR body and the changeset both declare `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so every non-prose path of the diff is in scope; nothing is a remainder for the lane seat.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `LocaleSchema`** — was any string; now `^[A-Za-z]{2,8}(?:-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$`, byte-identical to `SYS_USER_LOCALE_TAG_PATTERN` (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts:33`). Refused from now on: an underscore separator, surrounding or inner whitespace, the empty string, a language name, a one-letter language subtag (BCP-47 private-use `x-…` and grandfathered `i-…` tags), any subtag over 8 characters. **Right.** A session's `sys_user.locale` cannot name any of those either, so no translation stored under them was ever askable. Case is not judged; `resolveLocale` (`memory-i18n.ts:47`) folds case, so `zh-cn` resolves and refusing it would refuse a working locale. **Right.** Syntax only: `value-domain.zod.ts:82` records why no membership domain exists. **Right.**

2. **Reach of the narrowing** — re-measured on `main`: the complete consumer set of `LocaleSchema` is `TranslationItemSchema.locale`, the `TranslationBundleSchema` and `PlatformTranslationBundleSchema` map keys, `TranslationConfigSchema.defaultLocale / supportedLocales / fallbackLocale`, `Seed.locale[]` (`data/seed.zod.ts:213`) and `SeedLoaderConfig.locale` (`data/seed-loader.zod.ts:285`). The PR body names every one and states its scope; all six narrow through the one schema edit. `PackageLocaleSchema` (marketplace) is its own schema and is rightly untouched. The three readers the premise check named (registry.ts walks, lint-liveness, ui clientValidation) judge bundle shape structurally, not by key spelling, so they need no edit. **Right**, with one wording nit: the registry.ts comments at the submitLabel and subCaption walks still say "`LocaleSchema` is an open string"; the reasoning they carry (the key set cannot be enumerated) still holds, but the phrase is now imprecise. Not blocking.

3. **Error envelope** — one `invalid_format` issue at path `locale` (item door) or one `invalid_key` at the offending key (bundle doors), message naming the shape and the release, no tracker number in the runtime string. The save door maps schema issues to `422 INVALID_METADATA` with `issues[{path, message, code}]` through the existing `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` plumbing, which this diff does not touch, so the card's expected envelope is met at the item door and at `defineTranslation` / `defineTranslationBundle` and on the bundle map key, as triage 6399808976 ordered. Pinned at the schema layer (`translation.test.ts`: ten refused values, four doors). **Right.** No HTTP-level pin was added; acceptable, since the door mapping is pre-existing and unchanged.

4. **Data at rest** — D2 `translation-locale-tag-canonicalized`, `toMajor: 18`, order 76 (orders 1–75 are taken; 76 is the next free slot), `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '18.1.0'` = the package's current stable label, exactly the rule in `conversions/types.ts` (sibling precedent at the same value). It rewrites only the two spellings with one tag they can have meant (`_` as separator, surrounding whitespace) and only when the result passes `LocaleSchema`; everything else is left as stored and reported through `context.reportTodo`. Bundle-key renames go through `renameKey` (`walk.ts:675`), which merges an identical twin and returns null on differing strings, which the conversion turns into a TODO rather than picking a winner. Reach: `translations[]` item locale and bundle keys, `i18n.*`, `data[].locale[]`. A legacy item without `locale` is not misread as a bundle (letters-only keys skipped). **Right.** All three stored-row seams (`database-loader.ts:884`, `authored-translation-sync.ts:172`, `protocol.ts:6447`) replay the chain with retired entries and none re-parses the row through the schema afterwards, so a residual non-tag row keeps loading as stored, is listed by `os migrate meta --stored`, and is refused at its next save, exactly as the D3 entry states. **Right.** Deployed rows cannot be measured from the repository; conversion plus TODO listing is the coverage. Non-test source re-measured on `main`: zero underscore, padded or empty locale literals feed the schema. Fixture: 7 notices, covers every reach. **Right.**

5. **D3 entry** `translation-locale-non-tag-refused` — matches `SemanticMigration`, `conversionIds` joins the D2 id, `surface` carries no backticks (rendered in a code span), `replacement` does (sibling practice). **Right.** The JOIN row in `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` is owed for an entry retired after the newest stable; present. **Right.**

6. **Public surface** — no export added or removed (`LOCALE_TAG_SHAPE` and `LOCALE_TAG_REFUSAL` are module-private); the `Locale` type stays `string`; `.describe()` unchanged, so no generated artifact moves. The head's `TypeScript Type Check` job (api-surface, docs, authorable-surface gates) is green. **Right.**

7. **Third copy of the tag regex** — platform-objects, service-messaging and now spec each spell it; the parity pin covers only the first two. Spec cannot import platform-objects, so a literal copy is the right direction; a parity pin naming the spec copy would close the loop. Non-blocking.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25822-locale-tag-shape.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the changeset and the PR body, BREAKING banner, FROM → TO mapping with the one-line fix, exactly one `adr-0087: registered` marker naming both ids. A value refused is `narrowed`, and the level follows the kind (at least minor), so `minor` is right; the title's `feat(spec)!` matches. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head. **Matches.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (two files outside the claim's surface, each forced by a red test): the claim comment 6410133283 was amended to carry both; answered.
- Dev deviation 2 (worktree built after the shared checkout was detached): process only, no effect on the diff; answered.
- Dev deviation 3 (model-free commit trailers): what AGENTS.md prescribes; answered.
- `open_questions`: none.
- Out-of-scope finding (dogfood full battery on the head: 1 red, `authz-probe-blind-spot` pinning `handleI18nRequest` at 3 after #25956 on `main`): not this diff (no runtime file touched), reported, and card #25988 now carries it. Battery was full (299 files, 2541 tests). For the landing seat: AGENTS.md's main-red rule holds until that card closes.
- Check-runs on the head: every required context is `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`; `Lint UI` skipped by the paths filter); no advisory failure.
- Advisory for the lane seat: the hand-written pages the drift check names (`content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`) do not yet state the tag shape; prose face, not part of this verdict.
